archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate attacker)
archetype.definition: A shotgun-based thrower whose value comes from 10-to-19-yard throws between the numbers, not from the quick game or from designed runs, with scrambles as a useful escape valve.

report.headline: Cleaner throws and real intermediate juice, but sacks and red-zone stalls cap him
report.take:
McCarthy arrived in New York off a rough 2025 in Minnesota: -0.102 EPA per play (50th of 63), a -5.7 CPOE and 12 interceptions in 10 games. He came on in relief of Jameis Winston in Week 6 and has started every game since Week 7, with the Giants 3-1 in those starts. On the surface, 0.039 EPA per dropback (22nd of 55) and 7.66 yards per attempt (14th) make him a slightly-above-average starter. What matters more is how far that is from what he was a year ago.

The change is accuracy and decision quality. His bad-throw rate has dropped from 21% to 12%, which now ranks 9th of 45. His interception rate is 1.4%, 15th of 55, from a quarterback who threw 12 picks a year ago. The profile is lopsided. Throws of 10+ air yards have added 26 EPA, while everything under 10 has cost 7.5. Intermediate throws run at +0.549 per attempt and the middle of the field at +0.538, and Isaiah Likely (+0.517 per target) has been the main beneficiary. When he works the seams and digs, the offense moves.

The weaknesses sit at the edges. He is rarely pressured (15.1%, 5th lowest), but when he is, 43.5% of those pressures become sacks, 42nd of 45. That isn't new: his pressure-to-sack rate was poor in Minnesota too, so treat it as a trait. It shows up on third down, where he converts 28.9% with six sacks. His 2.1% TD rate (46th) comes largely from a -0.696 EPA red-zone sample on only 12 plays, which is small enough to drift back up. Throws to the right side (-0.217) and from under center (-0.206) have also been bad.

The last three games cooled things off: -0.022 EPA per dropback and a -4.4 CPOE. Part of that is the opponents. Jacksonville's No. 2 defense held him to a -13.9 CPOE game, and Philadelphia sacked him five times. Still, he is a 30-attempt starter in a run-leaning offense (pass rate over expected 27th) whose ceiling is set by volume and touchdowns rather than efficiency. The improvement looks real. A breakout does not.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws over the middle
strengths.body: Almost all of his passing value comes from 10+ air yards, and especially from throws into the 10-to-19 window. The middle of the field is where his completion rate and CPOE spike, which points to anticipation on in-breaking routes rather than luck on a few long balls. A 32-attempt sample is thin, but the shape matches his lower bad-throw rate, so it should mostly hold.

strengths.title: Turnover-worthy throws have dried up
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate fell from 21% last season to 12%, and his interception rate now sits in the top third of the league. That is the biggest real change from his Minnesota tape. It also explains why aggressive intermediate throws are paying off instead of turning into picks. The fact that it holds across four starts against varied defenses makes it more than a blip.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move chains
strengths.body: His designed runs have been a dead end, but his scrambles have been very productive. Nine scrambles produced six first downs at +0.818 EPA each. That is the useful half of his legs, and it is a stable habit, since he ran for 181 yards as a part-season starter last year.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: The line keeps him clean more than almost anyone, yet 43.5% of his pressures end in sacks. His rate was bottom-tier in 2025 as well, so this is how he plays rather than a fluke. The cost is concentrated where it hurts most: six of his 11 sacks came on third down, where the offense converts under 30%. These are not plays he is extending to create something; they are drive-killers.

concerns.title: Red-zone and TD drought
concerns.body: A 2.1% TD rate ranks 46th, and the red-zone passing has been very poor at -0.696 EPA per play. That is only 12 plays, so expect some recovery toward his 2025 TD rate. A run-leaning offense near the goal line limits how much.

concerns.title: Short game gives nothing back
concerns.body: Throws under 10 air yards and the screen game behind the line have cost value. The underneath work for Malik Nabers has also been barely positive despite his team-high target total. When defenses take away the middle-depth window, there isn't an efficient short game to fall back on. That is the main risk to his efficiency holding up.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung from strong outings against Houston and Washington to negative games against Philadelphia (five sacks) and Jacksonville (-13.9 CPOE). As a result, the last three games trail his season efficiency even though his yardage per game is up.

nextGame.headline: Colts' corner-less secondary invites shots, but a lead may shrink volume
nextGame.body:
Indianapolis is a middling pass defense (18th in EPA allowed) that gives up explosive passes at the 29th-ranked rate. It is also below average on short throws, and opposing tight ends have produced well against it. That fits his best area, the intermediate middle, and his best target, Isaiah Likely. The catch is game script. The Giants are 6.5-point favorites against the league's worst passing offense, and offenses already run more than usual against this defense. His splits when leading by 9+ have been poor, and his team leans on the run.

Availability tilts things further. Both of Indianapolis's starting corners, Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, are out, which removes the backbone of the coverage he'd face on outside and intermediate throws. Colts left and right tackles Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis are also out, which should help the Giants' defense hand him short fields. On his side, the only listed injury is a little-used backup back on IR, so his weapons are intact.

keyMatchups.title: Missing starting corners
keyMatchups.body: With Ward and Gardner both out, backups will cover the throws he has thrived on. A defense already allowing explosive passes at a high rate gets thinner. This is the clearest edge of the week.

keyMatchups.title: Likely against a soft TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Indianapolis ranks near the bottom against the top tight end, both in EPA allowed and in points over average. Likely has been his most efficient target by a wide margin. Seam and over-the-middle throws to him are the likeliest route to a big game.

keyMatchups.title: Lead-protecting game script
keyMatchups.body: The Colts' pass offense ranks last, and opponents already tilt run-heavy against them. A Giants lead would cut his attempts. His play when ahead by 9+ has been his worst state, though that is a 24-play sample.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Giants keep throwing between the numbers to Likely once they're ahead, or go into run-and-checkdown mode, where his EPA disappears.

restOfSeason.body:
The improvement in accuracy and ball security looks like the real thing: the bad-throw and interception changes are too large to call noise. Expect him to stay a modestly positive-EPA starter. His per-game output will be capped by a run-leaning offense that has kept him around 30 attempts, and by sacks he takes rather than avoids. The TD rate should recover somewhat as the small red-zone sample evens out. His deep and intermediate efficiency will likely cool as more tape on him accumulates.

Projected per game: roughly 180-235 passing yards, 0.7-1.3 passing TDs and 15-30 rushing yards on about 26-33 attempts. Some of that rushing comes from scrambles that move the chains.
swingFactors: How often game script lets the Giants throw

confidence.note: Only four starts and 142 attempts, on a new team, after a poor 2025.
